correctness.rationale: For n=p^a q^b with p<q, gamma(n)^2|sigma(n) forces p^2|sigma(q^b) and q^2|sigma(p^a). The second condition forces a>=3. If a+b<=5, only b=1 or 2 remains. The b=2 case forces a=3 and contradicts the factorization sigma(p^3)=(p+1)(p^2+1). For b=1, a=3 is excluded by q>=p^2-1 plus an exact size inequality, while a=4 forces q=p^2-1, impossible except p=2,q=3, where 9 does not divide 31. The witness 96 has gamma(96)^2=36, sigma(96)=252, and Omega(96)=6.
